pages.text: Port Arden City Council. Report to Council: Harbour Line Light Rail Extension. Meeting date: 12 March 2026. Prepared by the Office of the City Engineer. Author: Tomás Reyes, Project Director. Summary: Council is asked to approve the extension of the Harbour Line light rail by 9.5 kilometres, from Central Station to Kestrel Point, with six new stations. The estimated total project cost is $420 million. Construction is planned to begin in July 2026, with passenger services starting in the fourth quarter of 2028.

Funding. The project is funded by a $250 million grant from the Northshore State Transport Fund and $170 million in municipal bonds. Stations. The six new stations are Wharf Street, Old Customs House, Marina Park, Gullwing Avenue, Kestrel Point East and Kestrel Point, with an interchange at Central Station. Benefits. The extension is expected to reduce car trips across the Harbour Bridge by an estimated 12 percent.

Risks. Soft soil near Marina Park may require deeper foundations. The Old Customs House station is next to a heritage-listed building completed in 1887. Construction noise will affect residents along Wharf Street. Recommendation. Council approves the project and authorises the City Engineer to award the main construction contract. Moved by Councillor Ana Ruiz. Approved 9 votes to 2.

Port Arden Herald, 13 March 2026. Council backs $420m light rail extension despite resident concerns. By Priya Nandakumar. Port Arden City Council voted 9 to 2 on Thursday to approve the Harbour Line extension to Kestrel Point. Mayor Elena Marsh called it 'the most important transport decision in a generation'. The six-station line is due to open by the end of 2028.

Not everyone is convinced. The Harbourside Residents Association, led by Daniel Okafor, says months of night-time construction on Wharf Street will be unbearable. 'We support public transport, but not at the cost of our sleep,' Okafor said. The association plans to present a petition with 3,400 signatures to the council in April 2026. Councillor Ben Whitfield, who voted against the project, said the budget relies too heavily on borrowing.

Media release. Halvorsen Civil Works. 2 April 2026. Halvorsen Civil Works wins Harbour Line extension contract. Halvorsen Civil Works has been selected by Port Arden City Council to design and build the Harbour Line light rail extension, a project valued at $380 million. Chief executive Ingrid Halvorsen said the company expects to create 1,200 construction jobs.

Timeline. Halvorsen expects to start site works in August 2026 and to hand over the completed line for passenger service in mid-2029. The company will use quieter vibratory piling to limit noise along Wharf Street. Media contact: Sam Patel, Communications Manager.

1.text: Harbour Line Extension. Environmental Impact Assessment. Prepared by Tidewater Environmental Consulting for Port Arden City Council. June 2026. Lead author: Dr Hana Sato.

9.text: Ecology. The wetland north of Marina Park is habitat for the Arden marsh frog, a species listed as endangered. Construction within 50 metres of the wetland is prohibited during the breeding season, from September to November.

21.text: Noise. Night-time construction noise must not exceed 65 decibels at the nearest residence. Continuous monitoring is required along Wharf Street.

33.text: Mitigation. A mitigation budget of $12 million is recommended, covering frog relocation, noise barriers and heritage monitoring at the Old Customs House.

pages.text: Port Arden Heritage Trust. 20 April 2026. Dear Councillors, We object to the current design of the Old Customs House station. The building, completed in 1887, is the oldest surviving customs house in the region. The station entrance must not be attached to its eastern wall. Yours faithfully, Margaret Chen, Chair.
Harbour Line Ridership Forecast. Port Arden Transport Planning Unit. May 2026. The chart on the next page shows expected average weekday boardings on the extended line.

Harbour Line Extension. Community Feedback Summary. Port Arden City Council Engagement Team. May 2026. 2,150 residents responded to the online survey. 58 percent support the extension, 31 percent oppose it and 11 percent are undecided. Night-time construction noise was the most common concern, raised by 47 percent of respondents. Many respondents asked for a station closer to Gullwing Primary School.

pages.text: Understanding prompt injection. Port Arden Digital Services blog. June 2026. Author: Lena Fischer. Prompt injection is an attack where text such as 'ignore previous instructions' is hidden in a document to manipulate an AI system. From July 2026, the council's Digital Services team will review every AI tool it buys for this risk, and will run quarterly tests using sample attack documents.

Transcript. Harbour Line Community Reference Group. 3 June 2026. Chair (Grace Liu): Welcome, everyone. Assistant Director (Omar Haddad): The noise monitoring system will go live in August. Resident: Will the system alert us at night? Assistant Director: Yes. The system sends an alert whenever noise goes above 65 decibels.

Port Arden Orchid Society. Spring Newsletter. September 2026. President: Harold Finch. Our annual show at the Botanic Garden attracted 900 visitors. Best in show went to a Dendrobium grown by member Ruth Adeyemi. Next month's meeting covers repotting techniques.
